- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., > +1.5) and price is falling, model underreacts — add 2–3% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — apply +1.5–2.5% bias to short-term forecasts.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– > 0.5), model overfits noise — smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values before applying trend.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 5–7 days after a spike, model fails to recognize — reduce forecast by 2–4% in next 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates volatility — apply 10–15% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
